title: Inside Edition Spotlights Maine's Cryptozoology Collection, Largest Of Its Kind
excerpt: Bangor's new home for cryptozoology enthusiasts, The International Cryptozoology Museum, featured on national newsmagazine show.
content:
For over 30 years, Americans have tuned in to the national syndicated newsmagazine program Inside Edition for pop culture, celebrity scoops, and a broader look at the unique stories emerging from small towns across the nation.

This month, the program featured a Bangor-based museum, putting the Queen City on the map for something other than its connection to Stephen King! (Not that that's a bad thing at all.)

The International Cryptozoology Museum, formerly based out of Portland, officially opened a new spot on Broadway in Bangor this past spring.

Read More: The Fascinating World Of Cryptids At Bangor's New Museum

Offering folks from Eastern Maine and beyond a look at everything from Bigfoot's footprint casts to models of the Figi Mermaid or a Chupacabra, this museum specializes in what most would consider oddities. The unusual nature of these exhibits caught the attention of Inside Edition's producers, just in time for the Halloween season.

"Looking for a Halloween-appropriate road trip? The International Cryptozoology Museum in Bangor, Maine, is home to hundreds of casts of mysterious footprints that may or may not belong to Bigfoot! Whether you're a true believer or a skeptic, the collection is sure to spark some curiosity. And as assistant director Christopher Packard tells Inside Edition Digital, even fake footprints can make for a good story."

In the piece, Packard explains that the museum is the oldest and largest of its kind, with more than 20,000 items on display.

Read More: The Mystery Of Bigfoot: Maine's Unusual Sightings Explained

He says that "Cryptozology is the science that explores the edge of science."

Packard says the museum doesn't just have exhibits that could absolutely be real, but also things that are hoaxes, too.
